title: EU and India conclude talks on India joining Horizon Europe
dek: Association is envisaged for January 2027. Indian organisations would then be able to receive funding directly and lead Pillar II collaborative projects.
key_facts: Exploratory talks from 6 February 2026; formal talks from 17 July 2026
Formal signature, once both sides complete their procedures
body: The European Commission and India have finished negotiating India's association to Horizon Europe, the EU's research and innovation programme for 2021–2027. Association is the closest form of cooperation open to countries outside the EU, and it is envisaged to apply from January 2027.

Once the agreement is in force, organisations based in India would be able to receive Horizon Europe funding directly and to lead collaborative projects under Pillar II, which covers global challenges and European industrial competitiveness. Areas highlighted for joint work include health, digital technologies, industry, space, climate, energy and the bioeconomy.

The arrangements do not yet apply. Closing the negotiations clears the way for the agreement to be signed, which depends on both sides completing their internal procedures. The talks began with exploratory discussions on 6 February 2026, and formal negotiations opened on 17 July 2026.
why: For European consortia, this widens the pool of partners that can take part on equal terms with EU organisations. Indian universities, research bodies and companies are likely to start appearing more often in Pillar II proposals, including as coordinators. Teams planning for 2027 calls should talk to Indian partners early, but should not count on the new terms until the agreement has entered into force. Until then, the current participation rules for India continue to apply.
